youtube.title: C++ Inheritance: Constructor and Destructor Order | C++ Programming EP 62
youtube.description: In this episode you will predict the order of constructors, pass arguments to the base constructor and predict the order of destructors, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Constructor and destructor order · 0:55 Build and destroy · 1:35 Life of a Derived object · 2:05 Second program · 3:05 Recap · 3:35 Bug of the Day · 4:23 Challenge · 4:44 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we learn who is built first. The order matters a lot when classes depend on each other.

scenes.onScreen: "Constructor and destructor order": numbered lines (1. The base is built first; 2. The derived part is built next; 3. Destruction runs in the reverse order) and an analogy card: building a house: the foundation comes first, and the roof comes last
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: When you make a derived object, the base part is built first. Then the derived part is built. When the object dies, the order reverses. The derived part goes first, and then the base part. To give arguments to the base constructor, call it in the initializer list. Think of building a house. The foundation comes first, and the roof comes last. Taking it down reverses the order.
points: The derived part is built next
Destruction runs in the reverse order

scenes.narration: Follow the flow. The base is built first. Then the derived part. At the end, the derived part is destroyed first. The base part is destroyed last. The derived part may depend on the base part, so the base must live longer.

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

args.cpp: In constructor 'Dog::Dog()':
args.cpp:14:11: error: no matching function for call to 'Animal::Animal()'
   14 |     Dog() {}
      |           ^
args.cpp:9:5: note: candidate: 'Animal::Animal(std::string)'
    9 |     Animal(string name) : name_(name) {}
bug.why: The base part must be built first. If the base has no default constructor, the derived constructor must say which one to call.

pun: "The base class was always first in line. It said, I was here before you were derived."
challenge: Write three classes: A, B inherits from A, and C inherits from B. Print a message in each constructor. Predict the order for a C object.
challengeAnswer: A is built first, then B, then C. The destructors run in the reverse order: C, then B, then A.
